title: Choose ShipBrief’s visual world
question: The roll assigned Dispatch Strips. Keep it, choose an alternate, or reroll. This sets the visual language for every current view while keeping the existing workflows intact.

options.label: Dispatch Strips
options.lineage: Flight dispatch boards and paper flight progress strips
options.thesis: Each incoming push travels along a dimensional rail from linked evidence to human review.
options.viewport: A luminous 3D marker travels the dispatch rail above the push queue; selecting a strip opens linked commits beside a reviewable draft.
options.risk: Motion could distract from reading; transitions stay short and tied to real state changes.

raised.raise: A strict underlying grid keeps every strip, evidence row, and review action aligned with typographic precision.
Compact semantic status labels preserve the speed and precision builders expect, without inheriting a generic dark console.
The board gains disciplined page-like grouping so six views remain legible as one system.
A single material world carries consistently across navigation, evidence, and review surfaces.
Push-to-approval progression is shown as a clear sequence, with time and state readable at a glance.
One high-contrast amber signal marks the next decision without turning the whole interface into signage.

options.label: Annotated Release Proof
options.lineage: Editorial proof sheets and annotated technical field notes
options.thesis: A release is a dimensional proof: linked code evidence on the margin, marketing copy in the body.
options.viewport: A dimensional paper stack turns toward the selected push; margin tabs link draft passages to commits, with review controls at the decision point.
options.risk: Can privilege proofing aesthetics over quick orientation if every surface performs the metaphor.

options.label: Signals Instruments Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: The release queue reads like a live departures board, each change headed somewhere.
options.viewport: A small 3D split-flap module pivots from PUSH to REVIEW above a sortable queue of fixed-width rows and linked evidence.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: pushes become arrivals and drafts become destinations; strong audience recognition, slightly weaker evidence clarity.
options.risk: Can turn into decorative motion if fixed-cell discipline and readable evidence are lost.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The release history becomes a precise grid that turns code activity into readable structure.
options.viewport: A 3D grid sculpture moves one highlighted block from commit to draft above a modular evidence-and-review field.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: its grid makes the six views and evidence relationships explicit; audience identification is narrower than the assigned workflow metaphor.
options.risk: Can prioritize typographic display over comfortable long-form draft editing.

options.label: Yellow Wayfinding
options.lineage: Airport terminal signs and route maps
options.thesis: The next safe step is always unmistakable, from incoming push to draft approval.
options.viewport: A 3D route rail stages Push, Evidence, Draft, and Review; a moving light marks the active step above linked evidence and draft.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: excellent action clarity and a memorable signal color; weaker at showing the full evidence detail without a second surface.
options.risk: The high-contrast signal can overwhelm the content if used as a full-screen field.

options.label: Digital Design Canon Dark Console
options.lineage: Developer consoles and code review tools
options.case: Fuses poorly: the incumbent already reads as a generic developer console, so this would not establish a new world.
options.kept: Compact, precise semantic state labels and information density.

options.label: Pop Culture Shelf Catalog
options.lineage: Pastel character-goods catalogs and ranked shelves
options.case: Fuses poorly: the shelf and mascot framing obscures the evidence-led review job.
options.kept: A clear, scannable entry hierarchy for new pushes.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.lineage: Laban movement notation and dance scores
options.case: Fuses poorly: the notation language is unfamiliar to builders and marketing reviewers.
options.kept: A visible chronological progression from push through review.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, conventional SaaS workspace, executed with crisp hierarchy and quiet confidence.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar app shell puts pending draft review first, with evidence, activity, repositories, and settings one click away.
canonCard.risk: Intentionally familiar; the interface itself carries little distinctive identity.
